title: Tier-cap transition launch playbook: staggered limits, docs, and sales enablement
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Coordinate the rollout of revised pricing tiers and per-account limits ('Tier Caps') across hosted and dedicated customers, align billing enforcement with SKU mapping, and deliver synchronized release notes, in-product messaging, and sales enablement. This ticket owns cross-functional orchestration: PRD finalization, release-note drafts, billing/usage migration schedule, customer comms cadence, support runbook, and enablement materials for Sales and CSM. Workstreams: 1) SKU/limits mapping and backend enforcement (ENG). 2) Billing migration and invoice preview (Billing). 3) Console UI labels and quota UX (Console). 4) Release notes and public comms (Comms/Docs). 5) Sales/CS enablement (GTM). 6) Support playbook and SLO exceptions (Support/Trust).
checklist: Finalize SKU-to-tier mapping matrix and export to billing team
Confirm gating flags and feature toggles for staged enforcement
Draft release notes and coordinate legal review for pricing language
Create customer-facing FAQ and in-console banner copy
Prepare invoice preview job and sample invoices for top 20 customers
Ship training deck and one-pager for Sales + CSMs

release_notes_draft:
Release notes (short):
We are simplifying pricing tiers and introducing firm per-account caps to improve predictability and reduce unexpected overages. Customers will see updated SKU names and a preview of how new caps affect their usage in the Billing console prior to enforcement. Migration windows will be staggered; no immediate invoice changes until the preview period ends. For more details, see the full FAQ and migration timeline.

Release notes (long):
- What changed: consolidated several legacy SKUs into three tier families (Basic, Scale, Enterprise). Each tier has a clearly defined per-account cap and a recommended burst limit for short spikes.
- Why: to simplify purchasing decisions, reduce billing surprises, and enable clearer autoscaling behavior.
- When: customers will enter a 14-day preview period where they can see projected billing and receive a migration recommendation. Enforcement begins one week after preview for each cohort.
- Action for customers: Review your invoice preview in Console > Billing > Migration Preview and contact your account team if you need a custom limit.
- Contact: billing@redwood.ai and your assigned CSM for account-specific questions.
communications_plan: High-level comms: 1) Internal pre-brief (Mar 06): Exec summary to Sales, Support, Legal, and Infra. 2) Beta cohort comms (Mar 10): targeted email + in-console preview for customers flagged as heavy users. 3) Public announcement (Mar 20): blog post + release notes + updated pricing page. 4) Reminder and enforcement notices during each cohort's 14-day preview window. Channels: email, in-console banner, release notes, support portal, partner Slack. Legal sign-off required for public pricing language. For enterprise contracts, Sales rep outreach is required prior to enforcement.
sales_enablement_tasks: Build slide deck: value props, comparison table, migration talking points
Create objection-handling playbook (billing scenarios, contract exceptions)
Host two 60-min training sessions for AE/AM teams (Mar 12 & Mar 16)
Populate playbook in Sales wiki and link within CRM (SFDC playbook)
Prepare email templates for reps to use when contacting impacted customers
rollout_schedule: Mar 06: Internal pre-brief and blackout window defined
Mar 10: Beta cohort (50 customers) preview enabled; sample invoices sent
Mar 17: Beta feedback triage; adjust thresholds if >10% false positives
Mar 20: Public release notes and pricing page update; cohort A preview starts
Mar 27: Cohort A enforcement begins if no critical issues
Apr 03: Cohort B preview; ongoing monitoring
Apr 17: Full enforcement for remaining accounts (target)
metrics_to_track: % of accounts that view invoice preview
# of support tickets related to pricing/migration per day
Revenue delta attributable to tier changes (weekly)
Number of contract exceptions requested and approved
rollback_criteria: Rollback to previous cap enforcement if any cohort experiences: 1) >5% of previewed customers reporting incorrect invoice projections identified by regression testing AND 2) system-side error rate (billing pipeline exceptions) >1% sustained for 2 hours. Rollback procedure: disable enforcement flag, notify affected accounts, revert invoices in staging, escalate to SRE and Billing engineers. Final approval to re-attempt requires cross-functional sign-off (PM, Eng, Billing, Support).
